In the pentagon $ABCDE$ shown above, find $x.$
question.worked_solution:
A pentagon has $n=5$ sides. Therefore, the sum of the interior angles of a pentagon must be 

$$
\begin{aligned}{180}^{∘}\cdot (n-2) & ={180}^{∘}\cdot (5-2) \\  & ={180}^{∘}\cdot 3 \\  & ={540}^{∘}.\end{aligned}
$$

Adding up the internal angles and solving for $x,$ we get

$$
\begin{aligned}m∠A+m∠B+m∠C+m∠D+m∠E & ={540}^{∘} \\ {127}^{∘}+(2x)+(2x+{18}^{∘})+{110}^{∘}+(3x+{5}^{∘}) & ={540}^{∘} \\ 7x+{260}^{∘} & ={540}^{∘} \\ 7x & ={280}^{∘} \\ x & ={40}^{∘}.\end{aligned}
$$
